root_cause: Sparks from hot work (air carbon arc gouging of catwalk grating, without spark containment or continuous gas monitoring) ignited flammable hydrocarbon vapour in the vapour space of a badly corroded spent-acid tank that had holes in its roof and shell and was inadequately inerted through a temporary hose; the internal deflagration tore the shell from the floor. Mechanical integrity deferrals, the unreviewed change to spent-acid service and the unacted unsafe-condition report allowed it.
match_phrases: hot work ignites flammable vapour in tank
what_happened: After lunch the crew moved from TK-6 toward TK-3, gouging without a retest; with temperature reaching 85 F, at about 13:30 TK-3 exploded, lifted off its pad and fell, pulling down the catwalk; TK-6's withdrawal line broke; acid released and hydrocarbons burned for about half an hour.
consequence: 1 contractor killed and 8 injured; about 1.1 million gal of acid released, overwhelming the dike and sewers, with about 99,000 gal reaching the river and a fish kill.
missed_by_original_review: Mechanical integrity: repeated internal-inspection recommendations deferred and known leak unrepaired; no MOC for the change to spent-acid service and undersized temporary inerting; hot work programme allowed work near tanks with holes and flammable vapour without monitoring; UCR not acted on; MSDS classed spent acid as non-combustible.

source.reference: US Chemical Safety Board, Investigation Report: Refinery Incident, Motiva Enterprises LLC, Delaware City Refinery, Delaware City, Delaware, July 17, 2001; Report No. 2001-05-I-DE, October 2002. https://www.csb.gov/assets/1/20/Motiva_Final_Report.pdf
